title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 7. The Childhood Plays
html:
The story of Vishvarupa: his sannyasa and the parents' blessing; Vishvambhara's promise to serve His parents; His pranks and the dream of Jagannatha Mishra; Vishvambhara asks His mother not to eat on Ekadashi; the question of Damodara

Verse 1

इति श्रुत्वा हरेः पादपङ्कजध्याननिर्वृतः।
दामोदरः पर्यपृच्छद्धरेर्ज्येष्ठस्य सत्कथाम्॥१॥

iti śrutvā hareḥ pādapaṅkajadhyānanirvṛtaḥ|
dāmodaraḥ paryapṛcchaddharerjyeṣṭhasya satkathām||1||

iti — thus; shrutva — having heard; hareh — of Hari; pada-pankaja-dhyana-nirvritah — blissful in meditation on the lotus feet; damodarah — Damodara; paryaprichchhat — inquired; hareh — of Hari; jyeshthasya — of the elder (brother); sat-katham — the holy story.

1Having heard this, and blissful in meditation on Hari's lotus feet, Damodara asked to hear the holy story of Hari's elder brother:

Verse 2

कथयस्व महत्ख्यातं विश्वरूपस्य तत्त्वतः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा प्राह भो ब्रह्मञ्छ्रूयतां कथयामि ते॥२॥

kathayasva mahatkhyātaṁ viśvarūpasya tattvataḥ|
tacchrutvā prāha bho brahmañchrūyatāṁ kathayāmi te||2||

kathayasva — tell; mahat — the great; khyatam — renowned (story); vishvarupasya — of Vishvarupa; tattvatah — truly; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; praha — said; bhoh brahman — O brahmana; shruyatam — listen; kathayami — I shall tell; te — to you.

2"Tell me truly the great and renowned story of Vishvarupa." Hearing this, (Murari) replied: "Listen, O brahmana, and I shall tell you."

Verse 3

इत्युक्त्वा वक्तुमारेभे वैद्यो हृद्यां कथां शुभाम्।
बलदेवांशकस्यापि विश्वरूपस्य पावनीम्॥३॥

ityuktvā vaktumārebhe vaidyo hṛdyāṁ kathāṁ śubhām|
baladevāṁśakasyāpi viśvarūpasya pāvanīm||3||

iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; vaktum — to tell; arebhe — began; vaidyah — the physician (Murari); hridyam — heart-charming; katham — the story; shubham — auspicious; baladeva-amshakasya — of the portion of Baladeva; api — also; vishvarupasya — of Vishvarupa; pavanim — purifying.

3With these words the physician1 began the heart-charming, auspicious and purifying story of Vishvarupa, the portion of Baladeva.

Verse 4

श्रीमच्छ्रीविश्वरूपः सकलगुणनिधिः षोडशाब्दोऽतिशुद्धः
प्रापाचार्यत्वमात्मश्रवणमननतः शक्तधीः प्रेमभक्तः।
सर्वज्ञः सर्वदासौ नरहरिचरणासक्तचित्तोऽतिहृष्टः
शान्तः सन्तोषयुक्तो जगति न रतिमान्वेदवेत्ता रसज्ञः॥४॥

śrīmacchrīviśvarūpaḥ sakalaguṇanidhiḥ ṣoḍaśābdo'tiśuddhaḥ
prāpācāryatvamātmaśravaṇamananataḥ śaktadhīḥ premabhaktaḥ|
sarvajñaḥ sarvadāsau naraharicaraṇāsaktacitto'tihṛṣṭaḥ
śāntaḥ santoṣayukto jagati na ratimānvedavettā rasajñaḥ||4||

shrimach-chhri-vishvarupah — Sriman Sri Vishvarupa; sakala-guna-nidhih — a treasury of all virtues; shodasha-abdah — sixteen years old; ati-shuddhah — utterly pure; prapa — attained; acharyatvam — the rank of acharya; atma-shravana-mananatah — by hearing and reflecting on the Self; shakta-dhih — of powerful intellect; prema-bhaktah — a devotee full of love; sarva-jnah — all-knowing; sarvada — always; asau — he; narahari-charana-asakta-chittah — with mind attached to the feet of Narahari; ati-hrishtah — very joyful; shantah — peaceful; santosha-yuktah — contented; jagati — to the world; na ratiman — not attached; veda-vetta — knower of the Vedas; rasa-jnah — knower of rasa.

4Sriman Sri Vishvarupa, a treasury of every virtue, utterly pure, became an acharya at sixteen by hearing of the Self and reflecting upon it. Of powerful intellect, a devotee full of love, all-knowing, he was ever joyful, his heart clinging to the feet of Narahari; peaceful and content, unattached to the world, he knew the Vedas and knew rasa.

Verse 5

जनको विजने विचिन्त्य तत्तनयस्योद्वहनोचितां वधूम्।
मनसा परिचिन्तयन्स्वयं बुबुधे तत्सकलं द्विजात्मजः॥५॥

janako vijane vicintya tattanayasyodvahanocitāṁ vadhūm|
manasā paricintayansvayaṁ bubudhe tatsakalaṁ dvijātmajaḥ||5||

janakah — the father; vijane — in private; vichintya — having considered; tat — that; tanayasya — of the son; udvahana-uchitam — fit for marriage; vadhum — a bride; manasa — in his mind; parichintayan — pondering; svayam — himself; bubudhe — knew; tat — that; sakalam — all; dvija-atmajah — the brahmana's son.

5In private the father was considering a suitable bride for his son; but the brahmana's son himself came to know all that he was pondering in his heart.

Verse 6

स विश्वरूपः पितुरित्थमन्तश्चेष्टां विदित्वा सकलं तितिक्षुः।
त्यक्त्वा गृहं स्वर्गनदीं प्रतीर्य जग्राह संन्यासमशक्यमन्यैः॥६॥

sa viśvarūpaḥ pituritthamantaśceṣṭāṁ viditvā sakalaṁ titikṣuḥ|
tyaktvā gṛhaṁ svarganadīṁ pratīrya jagrāha saṁnyāsamaśakyamanyaiḥ||6||

sah — that; vishvarupah — Vishvarupa; pituh — of the father; ittham — thus; antah-cheshtam — the inner intention; viditva — knowing; sakalam — all; titikshuh — forbearing; tyaktva — leaving; griham — home; svarga-nadim — the heavenly river (Ganga); pratirya — crossing; jagraha — took; sannyasam — sannyasa; ashakyam — impossible; anyaih — for others.

6Learning thus all his father's hidden intentions, the forbearing Vishvarupa left home, crossed the heavenly river and took sannyasa, which others cannot attain.

Verse 7

ततः पिता तत्परिश्रुत्य विह्वलो माता च साध्वी विललाप दुःखिता।
तावाहतुः पुत्रहितौ सुतो मे संन्यासधर्मे निरतो भवत्विति॥७॥

tataḥ pitā tatpariśrutya vihvalo mātā ca sādhvī vilalāpa duḥkhitā|
tāvāhatuḥ putrahitau suto me saṁnyāsadharme nirato bhavatviti||7||

tatah — then; pita — the father; tat — that; parishrutya — hearing; vihvalah — overwhelmed; mata — the mother; cha — and; sadhvi — virtuous; vilalapa — lamented; duhkhita — grieving; tau — the two; ahatuh — said; putra-hitau — wishing their son well; sutah — son; me — my; sannyasa-dharme — in the dharma of sannyasa; niratah — devoted; bhavatu — may he be; iti — thus.

7When he heard of this, the father was overwhelmed, and the virtuous mother wept bitterly. But then both, wishing their son well, said: "May our son remain true to the dharma of sannyasa!"

Verse 8

इत्याशिषस्तौ तनयाय दत्त्वा मुनिव्रतौ धैर्यमुवाहतुः स्म।
विषादमुत्सृज्य सुतं जगत्पतिं क्रोडे निधायाशु मुदं तदापतुः॥८॥

ityāśiṣastau tanayāya dattvā munivratau dhairyamuvāhatuḥ sma|
viṣādamutsṛjya sutaṁ jagatpatiṁ kroḍe nidhāyāśu mudaṁ tadāpatuḥ||8||

iti — such; ashishah — blessings; tau — the two; tanayaya — to their son; dattva — giving; muni-vratau — observing the vow of sages (silence); dhairyam — fortitude; uvahatuh sma — maintained; vishadam — grief; utsrijya — casting off; sutam — the son; jagat-patim — the Lord of the world; krode — on the lap; nidhaya — placing; ashu — at once; mudam — joy; tada — then; apatuh — attained.

8Having given their son this blessing, both kept their fortitude like sages; casting off grief, they took their son — the Lord of the world — onto their laps and at once were filled with joy.

Verse 9

ततो हरिः प्राह पितर्गतो मे भ्राता भवन्तं परिहाय दूरम्।
मयैव कार्या भवतश्च सेवा मातुश्च नित्यं सुखमाप्नुहि त्वम्॥९॥

tato hariḥ prāha pitargato me bhrātā bhavantaṁ parihāya dūram|
mayaiva kāryā bhavataśca sevā mātuśca nityaṁ sukhamāpnuhi tvam||9||

tatah — then; harih — Hari; praha — said; pitah — O father; gatah — has gone; me — my; bhrata — brother; bhavantam — you; parihaya — leaving; duram — far; maya — by me; eva — indeed; karya — will be done; bhavatah — to you; cha — and; seva — service; matuh — to the mother; cha — and; nityam — always; sukham — happiness; apnuhi — obtain; tvam — you.

9Then Hari said: "Father, My brother has left you and gone far away. It is I who will serve you and mother — and may you always be happy."

Verse 10

इत्थं निशम्य स्वसुतस्य वाक्यमनल्पगम्भीरमनोज्ञमर्थवत्।
आलिङ्ग्य तं हर्षजनेत्रवारिभिरवाप मोदं जननी पिता च॥१०॥

itthaṁ niśamya svasutasya vākyamanalpagambhīramanojñamarthavat|
āliṅgya taṁ harṣajanetravāribhiravāpa modaṁ jananī pitā ca||10||

ittham — thus; nishamya — hearing; sva-sutasya — of their son; vakyam — the speech; analpa-gambhira-manojnam — weighty, deep, charming; arthavat — meaningful; alingya — embracing; tam — him; harsha-ja-netra-varibhih — with tears of joy in their eyes; avapa — attained; modam — delight; janani — the mother; pita — the father; cha — and.

10Hearing such words from their son — weighty, deep, charming and full of meaning — the mother and father embraced Him and, with tears of joy in their eyes, were filled with delight.

Verse 11

तदङ्गसंस्पर्शरसाभितृप्तगात्राणि नार्द्रा विदुरञ्जसापरम्।
गताः स्वयोगेन यथा सुयोगिनः पश्यन्ति नेमं न परं च लोकम्॥११॥

tadaṅgasaṁsparśarasābhitṛptagātrāṇi nārdrā vidurañjasāparam|
gatāḥ svayogena yathā suyoginaḥ paśyanti nemaṁ na paraṁ ca lokam||11||

tat-anga-samsparsha-rasa-abhitripta-gatrani — (their) limbs sated with the sweetness of touching his body; na — not; ardrah — moist (with tears); viduh — knew; anjasa — at all; aparam — anything else; gatah — absorbed; sva-yogena — by their own yoga; yatha — as; su-yoginah — accomplished yogis; pashyanti — see; na — neither; imam — this; na — nor; param — the other; cha — and; lokam — world.

11Their limbs were sated with the sweetness of His touch; bathed in tears, they knew nothing else — as accomplished yogis, absorbed in their own yoga, see neither this world nor the next.

Verse 12

पठन्पितुः सेवनयुक्तचेताः क्रीडापरो बालकसङ्घमध्ये।
क्रीडन्वयस्यैः किल धूलिधूसरो न वेद किंचित्क्षुधितोऽपि भोजनम्॥१२॥

paṭhanpituḥ sevanayuktacetāḥ krīḍāparo bālakasaṅghamadhye|
krīḍanvayasyaiḥ kila dhūlidhūsaro na veda kiṁcitkṣudhito'pi bhojanam||12||

pathan — studying; pituh — to his father; sevana-yukta-chetah — with mind engaged in service; krida-parah — intent on play; balaka-sangha-madhye — amid the band of boys; kridan — playing; vayasyaih — with companions; kila — indeed; dhuli-dhusarah — grey with dust; na veda — did not know (care for); kinchit — at all; kshudhitah — hungry; api — though; bhojanam — food.

12He studied, serving His father with all His heart, yet He was also caught up in play among a band of boys: romping with His companions, grey with dust, even when hungry He forgot all about food.

Verse 13

कदाचिदालोक्य पिता स्वतन्त्रं संभर्त्सयामास सुतं हितार्थी।
पाठादिकं चैव विहाय सर्वं क्षुधार्दितः क्रीडसि बालकैर्वृतः॥१३॥

kadācidālokya pitā svatantraṁ saṁbhartsayāmāsa sutaṁ hitārthī|
pāṭhādikaṁ caiva vihāya sarvaṁ kṣudhārditaḥ krīḍasi bālakairvṛtaḥ||13||

kadachit — once; alokya — seeing; pita — the father; svatantram — self-willed; sambhartsayamasa — scolded; sutam — the son; hita-arthi — desiring his good; patha-adikam — study and the rest; cha eva — and; vihaya — abandoning; sarvam — all; kshudha-arditah — tormented by hunger; kridasi — you play; balakaih — by boys; vritah — surrounded.

13Once, seeing his son so wilful, the father, wishing Him well, scolded Him: "You have thrown aside Your lessons and everything else, and You play with the boys though You are hungry!"

Verse 14

ततो रजन्यां शयनावसाने स्वप्नेऽवदत्तं द्विजवर्यमुख्यः।
न किं सुतं त्वं बहुमन्यसे हि किं वा पशुः स्पर्शमणिं न वेत्ति॥१४॥

tato rajanyāṁ śayanāvasāne svapne'vadattaṁ dvijavaryamukhyaḥ|
na kiṁ sutaṁ tvaṁ bahumanyase hi kiṁ vā paśuḥ sparśamaṇiṁ na vetti||14||

tatah — then; rajanyam — at night; shayana-avasane — at the end of sleep; svapne — in a dream; avadat — said; tam — to him; dvija-varya-mukhyah — the foremost of the best brahmanas; na kim — do not; sutam — the son; tvam — you; bahu-manyase — esteem highly; hi — indeed; kim va — or; pashuh — a beast; sparsha-manim — the touchstone; na vetti — does not know.

14Then at night, toward dawn, the foremost of the best brahmanas appeared to him in a dream and said: "Do you not value your son? Or are you like a beast that knows nothing of the worth of a touchstone?

Verse 15

रत्नांशुकालङ्कृतदेहयष्टिः किं वा न चाश्नाति तदंशुकानि।
तमाह मिश्रो ह्यकुतोभयः स्वयं नारायणश्चेद्भवतीह पुत्रः॥१५॥

ratnāṁśukālaṅkṛtadehayaṣṭiḥ kiṁ vā na cāśnāti tadaṁśukāni|
tamāha miśro hyakutobhayaḥ svayaṁ nārāyaṇaścedbhavatīha putraḥ||15||

ratna-amshuka-alankrita-deha-yashtih — (a beast) whose body is adorned with jewelled silks; kim va — does not; na — not; cha — and; ashnati — chew; tat-amshukani — those silks; tam — to him; aha — said; mishrah — Mishra; hi — then; akutobhayah — fearless; svayam — himself; narayanah — Narayana; chet — if; bhavati — is; iha — here; putrah — the son.

15Deck a beast's body in jewelled silks — will it not chew those silks?"2 Mishra fearlessly replied: "Even if my son is Narayana Himself,

Verse 16

तथापि तत्ताडनमेव धर्म इत्युक्तो विप्रोऽपि तमाह साधु।
इत्येवमुक्त्वा प्रययौ द्विजाग्र्यो वात्स्यः प्रबुद्धः पुनराशशंस॥१६॥

tathāpi tattāḍanameva dharma ityukto vipro'pi tamāha sādhu|
ityevamuktvā prayayau dvijāgryo vātsyaḥ prabuddhaḥ punarāśaśaṁsa||16||

tatha api — even so; tat-tadanam — punishing him; eva — indeed; dharmah — is duty; iti — thus; uktah — addressed; viprah — the brahmana; api — too; tam — to him; aha — said; sadhu — well (said); iti — thus; evam — so; uktva — having spoken; prayayau — departed; dvija-agryah — the foremost brahmana; vatsyah — the Vatsya; prabuddhah — awakening; punah — afterwards; ashashamsa — related (it).

16still it is my duty to punish Him." To this the brahmana said: "Rightly spoken." With these words the foremost of brahmanas departed, and the Vatsya, waking, told (of the dream).

Verse 17

स्वप्नं निशम्याशु जनाः प्रहृष्टा विश्वम्भरं पुरुषवर्यसत्तमम्।
तं मेनिरे पूर्णमनोरथं मुदा मेने पिता स्वं जननी च तुष्टा॥१७॥

svapnaṁ niśamyāśu janāḥ prahṛṣṭā viśvambharaṁ puruṣavaryasattamam|
taṁ menire pūrṇamanorathaṁ mudā mene pitā svaṁ jananī ca tuṣṭā||17||

svapnam — of the dream; nishamya — hearing; ashu — at once; janah — the people; prahrishtah — delighted; vishvambharam — Vishvambhara; purusha-varya-sattamam — the best of the best of men; tam — him; menire — considered; purna-manoratham — the fulfilment of (their) hopes; muda — joyfully; mene — considered; pita — the father; svam — his own (son); janani — the mother; cha — and; tushta — was satisfied.

17Hearing of the dream, the people rejoiced and joyfully saw in Vishvambhara, the best of the best, the fulfilment of their hopes; but the father considered Him his own son, and the mother was content.

Verse 18

ततः कदाचिन्निवसन्स्वमन्दिरे समुद्यदादित्यकरातिलोहितः।
स्वतेजसापूरितदेह आबभौ उवाच मातर्वचनं कुरुष्व मे॥१८॥

tataḥ kadācinnivasansvamandire samudyadādityakarātilohitaḥ|
svatejasāpūritadeha ābabhau uvāca mātarvacanaṁ kuruṣva me||18||

tatah — then; kadachit — once; nivasan — staying; sva-mandire — in his house; samudyat-aditya-kara-ati-lohitah — red as the rays of the rising sun; sva-tejasa-apurita-dehah — his body filled with his own splendour; ababhau — shone; uvacha — said; matah — mother; vachanam — the word; kurushva — do; me — my.

18Once, when He was at home, His body, red as the rays of the rising sun, blazed with its own light, and He said: "Mother, do as I tell you."

Verse 19

तथा ज्वलन्तं स्वसुतं स्वतेजसा विलोक्य भीता तमुवाच विस्मिता।
यदुच्यते तात करोमि तत्त्वया वदस्व यत्ते मनसि स्थितं स्वयम्॥१९॥

tathā jvalantaṁ svasutaṁ svatejasā vilokya bhītā tamuvāca vismitā|
yaducyate tāta karomi tattvayā vadasva yatte manasi sthitaṁ svayam||19||

tatha — so; jvalantam — blazing; sva-sutam — her son; sva-tejasa — with his own splendour; vilokya — seeing; bhita — frightened; tam — to him; uvacha — said; vismita — amazed; yat — what; uchyate — is said; tata — child; karomi — I will do; tat — that; tvaya — by you; vadasva — tell; yat — what; te — your; manasi — in mind; sthitam — is; svayam — yourself.

19Seeing her son blazing with His own light, the frightened and astonished mother said: "Child, whatever You say I shall do; tell me Yourself what is on Your mind."

Verse 20

तदित्थमाकर्ण्य वचोऽमृतं पुनस्तां प्राह मातर्न हरेस्तिथौ त्वया।
भोक्तव्यमाकर्ण्य वचः सुतस्य सा तथेति कृत्वा जगृहे प्रहृष्टवत्॥२०॥

taditthamākarṇya vaco'mṛtaṁ punastāṁ prāha mātarna harestithau tvayā|
bhoktavyamākarṇya vacaḥ sutasya sā tatheti kṛtvā jagṛhe prahṛṣṭavat||20||

tat — that; ittham — thus; akarnya — hearing; vachah-amritam — the nectar of speech; punah — again; tam — to her; praha — said; matah — mother; na — not; hareh — of Hari; tithau — on the lunar day; tvaya — by you; bhoktavyam — should be eaten; akarnya — hearing; vachah — the word; sutasya — of the son; sa — she; tatha — so be it; iti — thus; kritva — saying; jagrihe — accepted; prahrishtavat — joyfully.

20Hearing these words, sweet as nectar, He said to her: "Mother, on the day of Hari you must not eat."3 Hearing her son, she gladly agreed: "So be it."

Verse 21

निवेदितं पूगफलादिकं यद्द्विजेन भुक्त्वा पुनरब्रवीत्ताम्।
व्रजामि देहं परिपालयस्व सुतस्य निश्चेष्टगतं क्षणार्धम्॥२१॥

niveditaṁ pūgaphalādikaṁ yaddvijena bhuktvā punarabravīttām|
vrajāmi dehaṁ paripālayasva sutasya niśceṣṭagataṁ kṣaṇārdham||21||

Thus ends the seventh sarga, "The Childhood Plays" (Balya-krida), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. Murari Gupta was a physician (vaidya) by caste and occupation.
  2. The sense: you do not value your son, as a beast knows the worth neither of the touchstone nor of precious silk.
  3. The lunar day of Hari is Ekadashi, the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, a fast day.
  4. Yogamaya is the Lord's internal, spiritual energy, by which He Himself conceals or reveals Himself in His pastimes (cf. Bhagavad-gita 7.25: "I am not manifest to all, being veiled by yogamaya"). It is not the external maya that deludes living beings; the Lord is never subject to that.
